title: SQL-authoritative JSON asset lookup and bounded fallback failure

phases.objective: Resolve prior JSON assets through the configured SQL-primary data source without initializing Google Sheets, while preserving the original provider result when any secondary lookup fails.

e2e_journeys.actor: System tool dispatcher recording a failed GitHub provider execution
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: performUniversalServerWriteback with failed github_get_git_ref_head results under SQL and Sheets data-source modes
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: SQL mode reuses the latest active transported JSON asset without invoking Sheets, while Sheets lookup failure remains a bounded warning and neither path replaces the original provider error.
steps: Submit a failed GitHub provider result to universal writeback in Sheets mode and force the existing-asset lookup to throw the missing spreadsheet identifier error.
Verify that governed execution-log and JSON-asset evidence continue and that the provider failure remains authoritative.
Submit a second failed provider result in SQL mode and resolve matching JSON Asset Registry rows through the SQL-primary data-source adapter.
Select the latest active transported asset, suppress duplicate JSON-asset insertion, and prove that the injected Sheets lookup was never invoked.
Read back both writeback results, execution-log evidence, JSON-asset counts, lookup calls, and captured warnings.
assertions: Both returned status, error code, and short message values remain the original provider failure values.
Sheets mode does not invoke the SQL lookup and its missing spreadsheet error appears only as a bounded warning.
SQL mode invokes JSON Asset Registry findRows exactly once with asset_key and never invokes the Sheets lookup.
A SQL row with active_status 1 and a non-empty transport_status is accepted as the existing authoritative asset.
The Sheets failure path writes a JSON asset row, while the SQL existing-asset path avoids a duplicate row.
Each execution writes one Execution Log Unified row and preserves the governed pre-response log guard.

phases.objective: Add structured observability for SQL lookup latency, fallback classification, and degraded secondary writeback dependencies without changing provider authority.
Exercise SQL, Sheets fallback, storage, and execution-log dependency failures while proving bounded continuation and deterministic evidence.
Validate SQL-authoritative lookup and Sheets suppression against a live non-production runtime.
Verify exact Production SHA and runtime readback without intentionally disrupting production dependencies.
